skill.description: Guides custom PixiJS v8 rendering with GLSL and WGSL shaders, typed uniforms, filters, texture resources, batchers, and advanced GPU features.

security_audit.summary: All 94 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, JavaScript shader strings, API documentation links, or GLSL and TypeScript syntax. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or shell execution in the three reviewed documentation files. The CSP guidance describes a fallback synchronization path, not a request to weaken browser security.

content.user_title: Build Custom PixiJS v8 Shaders and Filters
content.value_statement: Custom PixiJS rendering requires precise shader bindings, uniform types, and renderer-specific resource handling. This skill provides patterns and references for building shaders, filters, and advanced GPU workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides Shader.from configuration for GLSL and WGSL programs with explicit entry points and resource bindings.
Explains typed UniformGroup values, array sizes, matrix formats, UBO layout constraints, and runtime synchronization.
Provides custom filter patterns, texture resource bindings, and destination sampling through blendRequired.
Documents partial GPU uploads, depth sampling, integer textures, 3D textures, array textures, and WebGPU storage textures.
Explains WebGPU override constants, custom bind group layouts, render bundle validation, and pooled scratch textures.
Outlines custom Batcher extensions and InstructionPipe cleanup for cached GPU resources.
limitations: Provides documentation and example fragments, not a standalone renderer, executable package, or automated test suite.
Targets PixiJS v8; some examples use APIs documented as introduced or changed in later v8 releases.
WebGPU-specific features require compatible browsers and devices; 3D and array textures require WebGL2 or WebGPU.
Shader placeholders, application setup, GPU testing, and custom batcher implementations require project-specific work.

output_examples.input: My PixiJS v8 shader reports that a uniform type is undefined.
output: The uniform declaration is missing its explicit type.
Define the time value as an f32 uniform inside a UniformGroup.
Match the resource name and uniform layout to the shader declaration.
Call update after changing values when the uniform group is static.

output_examples.input: My cached WebGPU draw bundle fails after I change render targets.
output: Render bundles retain attachment configuration, winding, and device compatibility from their recording pass.
Check bundle validity before replay and record a new bundle when compatibility changes.
Include render target changes and device loss in your validation.

output_examples.input: How should I upload a small changed range in a large vertex buffer?
output: Modify the relevant range in the CPU-side typed array.
Upload the changed byte length and byte offset through the buffer update method.
Keep byte offsets distinct from typed-array element indices.
An update without range arguments uploads the entire buffer.

best_practices: Match resource names, uniform types, field order, and shader entry points exactly.
Verify the installed PixiJS version and test each supported renderer with appropriate browser and GPU capabilities.
Validate bundles before replay, return scratch textures, and release cached GPU objects when instruction sets are destroyed.
anti_patterns: Using the removed positional Shader.from constructor or declaring uniforms without explicit types.
Placing textures in UniformGroup or using unsupported uniform types in UBO mode.
Replaying render bundles after target changes or device loss without checking validity.

faq.question: Which PixiJS version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets PixiJS v8. Some sections describe later v8 API changes, so check your installed release before applying examples.

faq.question: Can one shader support WebGL and WebGPU?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide GLSL programs for WebGL and WGSL programs for WebGPU, with matching entry points and resource bindings.

faq.question: Where should textures be bound?
faq.answer: Bind texture sources and sampler styles as top-level shader resources. Do not put textures inside UniformGroup.

faq.question: Does the skill run or test shaders automatically?
faq.answer: No. It supplies guidance and example fragments. You must integrate and test shaders in your application.

faq.question: How does strict CSP affect uniform buffers?
faq.answer: The skill recommends importing pixi.js/unsafe-eval at startup for the fallback synchronization path when CSP disallows dynamic function construction.

faq.question: Are advanced GPU features available on every renderer?
faq.answer: No. Storage textures and render bundles are WebGPU-specific. Three-dimensional and array textures require WebGL2 or WebGPU.
